before.title: 48V Mild-Hybrid (EQ Boost) Integrated Starter-Generator Failure
before.description: GLC 300 models with the M264 engine use a 48-volt mild-hybrid system with an Integrated Starter-Generator (ISG) mounted between the engine and transmission, fed by a small lithium-ion battery. The ISG, its 48V battery, or a loose/overheating 48V ground connection can fail, triggering a '48V On-Board Electrical System Malfunction' warning. Failures often cause a no-start condition that cannot be jump-started, stalling while driving, or in severe cases overheated connections posing a fire risk. Because the ISG sits between engine and gearbox, repair is labor-intensive and expensive.
before.solution: Diagnose the 48V circuit; remedies range from re-securing/replacing the 48V ground connection or the 48V lithium battery to replacing the ISG itself (which typically requires transmission removal). Address any related Mercedes 48V recall/service campaign for the affected connection.

citations.title: Mercedes C300, E350, GLC300 48V System Failure: ISG Guide - Go-Parts
A Guide to the Hybrid Integrated Starter-Generator in Mercedes-Benz Engines - Arrowhead MB

engines: M264 2.0L turbo I4 (EQ Boost mild hybrid)
proposal.title: 48V Mild-Hybrid (EQ Boost) Integrated Starter-Generator Failure

before.title: Cold-Start Camshaft Adjuster (Magnet/Solenoid) Rattle
before.description: On the M274/M264 2.0L turbo engines used in the GLC, the intake camshaft adjuster relies on an internal locking pin that wears over time. Without oil pressure at cold start, the adjuster fails to lock in its default position, producing a distinct metallic rattle for 2-4 seconds on a cold start. Oil leaking around the camshaft adjuster solenoid can also seep into the wiring harness and trigger timing faults. Left unrepaired it risks valve-timing errors and further engine wear.
before.solution: Replace the camshaft adjuster(s) and/or the camshaft magnet/solenoid actuators; use of fresh, correct-spec oil and addressing any oil-pressure deficiency is part of the fix. Verify no oil contamination has reached the solenoid connectors.
symptoms: Loud metallic rattle for 2-4 seconds on cold start

citations.title: Mercedes 2.0L M274/M264 Camshaft Adjuster Rattle & Failure (2014-2023) - Go-Parts
Need advice please! P0016, cold rattle on startup - MBWorld.org

proposal.title: Cold-Start Camshaft Adjuster (Magnet/Solenoid) Rattle

proposal.solution: Record the cold-start sound and duration and preserve camshaft-correlation, oil-pressure and mixture faults. Confirm the engine code, then separate camshaft adjustment, chain timing, valve-seat leakage, accessory drive and oil-pressure causes using the applicable Mercedes procedure. before.title: Crankcase Vent (PCV) Valve Failure with Engine Harness Oil Contamination
before.description: The integrated PCV / crankcase breather valve in the intake manifold (M274 2.0L turbo) commonly fails or its diaphragm tears, causing unmetered vacuum leaks. Oil mist can then migrate up the engine wiring harness via capillary action, contaminating connectors. Reported predominantly on 2016-2019 GLC 300 models. When ignored, lean running and loss of crankcase regulation risk further engine damage; in the worst cases the oil-soaked engine harness also requires replacement.
before.solution: Replace the PCV/crankcase ventilation valve (integrated into intake manifold/oil separator). If oil has wicked into the engine harness connectors, the affected harness section must also be replaced. Inspect connectors for oil intrusion at the same time.

proposal.title: Crankcase Vent (PCV) Valve Failure with Engine Harness Oil Contamination

Do not buy an intake line, PCV valve, harness or control unit from this page; eligibility and parts are VIN- and test-specific.

before.title: Diesel Timing Chain Tensioner Seal Oil Leak and Chain Stretch (OM651)
before.description: EU-spec GLC 220d/250d diesels with the OM651 engine are prone to a leaking timing chain tensioner sealing ring, which causes oil loss at the chain tensioner and can lead to timing chain stretch and rattle. Mercedes recalled over 100,000 OM651 vehicles in Germany over sealing-ring manufacturing tolerances (CDI models built Feb-Nov 2014). Owners also report related diesel ailments: piezo injector faults, swirl-flap linkage failure, EGR/DPF clogging and oil-cooler gasket leaks. If the chain stretches far enough, valve-timing damage can result.
before.solution: Replace the timing chain tensioner and its seal (and the chain if stretched); for affected build dates have the German/EU recall sealing-ring remedy performed. Address associated diesel items (swirl flap actuator, injectors, EGR/DPF, oil-cooler gasket) as diagnosed.
symptoms: Oil loss / drips near front of engine

before.title: Rear Brake Squeal and Premature Rear Pad Wear
before.description: Early X253 GLCs (2016-2019) are widely reported to squeal from the brakes, especially when backing up or in cold/damp weather, partly due to glazed pads and moisture trapped in drilled rotor holes. Separately, the rear brakes wear out noticeably before the fronts because the Electronic Parking Brake actuates the rear calipers each time the car is shut off. Mercedes updated the brake pads from the 2020 model year to address the squeal.
before.solution: Fit updated/quality (often aftermarket) brake pads to cure the squeal; clean/resurface or replace rotors as needed. Replace worn rear pads early and put the Electronic Parking Brake into service mode before any rear brake work to avoid damaging the actuators.
symptoms: Brake squeal, especially in reverse or cold weather
Rear pads worn out before fronts

proposal.title: Rear Brake Squeal and Premature Rear Pad Wear
proposal.description: The reviewed GLC communications do not establish the frozen combined rear-brake squeal and premature rear-pad-wear identity. Communication 10135720 supports front-axle squeal at low temperatures on early GLC 300 vehicles, not rear brakes. Distinguish normal friction noise from wear, contamination, hardware, caliper and parking-brake faults. Do not buy pads, rotors, calipers or parking-brake parts from this page; the frozen rear-wear identity and fitment are not established.
symptoms: wear and normal friction noise separated
